Hi Jonas,

I hope you're well — I'm Emily Stone, Associate Professor in Biology at Midstate University. Our lab is running an intensive summer project (student-focused, non-commercial) that requires burst inference for protein folding experiments. We evaluated Redwood during our pilot and it's the best fit for cost/latency.

We're a small group (PI + 2 grad students + 3 undergrads) and have exhausted the free trial credits assigned to our account. The Office of Research has a modest discretionary fund, but procurement timelines are slow and the compute need is time-sensitive (July-August).

Would Redwood be able to grant an exception top-up (one-off) of ~200k tokens worth of hosted credits to support the remainder of the summer run? I've attached the Office of Research award memo and a short one-page summary of the project and non-commercial status. We can provide any paperwork you need (certificate of non-commercial use, campus affiliation verification).

Attachments:
- midstate-award-letter.pdf (pdf, 72KB)

Thanks in advance — a quick yes/no would be great so we can plan.

Best,
Emily
